sentences.text: Rhombodus is a prehistoric ray belonging to the class Chondrichthyes and the family Rhombodontidae.
Scientists primarily know this genus from fossilized tail spines and unique rhombic teeth that are bilobate with vertical wrinkles and measure about 1.5 cm in width.
Individual species of this animal could grow to a length of 75 to 100 centimeters.
There are 126 recorded fossil occurrences of Rhombodus in the Paleobiology Database.

These rays lived between 70.6 and 55.8 million years ago, spanning the late Cretaceous and early Paleocene, with a time range extending from the Santonian to the Thanetian, approximately 85.7 to 56 million years ago.
Fossils have been found in sedimentary rocks across Africa, Europe, Asia, and the Americas.
